Antibiotic principles and resistance: 1

Choose the single best answer, then reveal the explanation.

A Gram-negative isolate acquires a plasmid encoding a beta-lactamase. The enzyme breaks down a susceptible antibiotic, while the bacterial cell-wall target remains functional. Which general resistance mechanism best describes this acquired trait?

  1. Modification of the drug target
  2. Increased drug efflux
  3. Reduced outer-membrane permeability
  4. Biofilm-associated persistence
  5. Enzymatic drug inactivation
Reveal answer and explanation
Correct answer

Enzymatic drug inactivation

Bacteria can produce enzymes that destroy or chemically modify an antibiotic.

Understanding the options

Enzymatic drug inactivation
Bacteria can produce enzymes that destroy or chemically modify an antibiotic.
Modification of the drug target
A changed target can bind the antibiotic less effectively while maintaining its microbial function. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.
Increased drug efflux
Transport pumps can lower intracellular antibiotic exposure. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.
Reduced outer-membrane permeability
Loss or alteration of porins can reduce entry of antibiotics into Gram-negative bacteria. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.
Biofilm-associated persistence
Organisms in biofilms can be difficult to eradicate; device management may be needed despite planktonic susceptibility. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.
